the-contract-and-its-binding.text: This page reports conformance evidence for the generic registry that cardano-keri consumes, bound to a pinned cardano-keri commit. The canonical identity rows carry the correction epic sixteen executed: a permissionless ledger cannot prohibit a rival registry, so canonical identity is a derivation the consumer authenticates, not a refusal the chain performs.

the-denominator.text: The inventory file carries forty-one rows with forty owned. Row CK zero six — bonds, poison, the juvenility window and the signature threshold — is recorded as out of scope: it belongs to cardano-keri's checkpoint machine, and is never claimed here.
The word executed never appears in the inventory file itself; a row prints as executed only when a run receipt for it exists and matches the current commit.

what-this-slice-executes.text: Three devnet sessions run in order on isolated nodes: generic registry rows, canonical identity rows, then the serialization boundary rows. Two checks compare Haskell values against the compiled blueprint and never start a node, and are never counted as devnet-executed.

the-generic-registry-rows.text: One cage, one key, four rows in order. Update folds and the new value reads back from the chain. Delete folds and the key proves absent. Re-insert folds and the third value reads back. Insert on the occupied key is refused by the state script, and a fresh cage accepting a valid insert proves the refusal discriminates.

Every accepting row carries a deliberately wrong variant the run requires to fail, and every refusal is attributed to the script that produced it. Had the chain accepted the occupied insert, that would be a finding, never relabelled as a refusal.

the-canonical-identity-rows.text: A designation split publishes the canonical seed. The first row boots the canonical registry and matches its token name against the SHA two fifty-six of the published seed's reference, recomputed locally. A second row initializes a rival registry from a second seed through the same bootstrap path.

The ledger accepts that rival — the acceptance is the finding, and it is asserted from the chain: both names read back and differ, and the canonical registry is untouched. The consumer's authentication rejects the rival on the derived name while accepting the canonical registry.

A control authenticator that checks only policy and address accepts the rival, which is what makes the rejection attributable to the name alone. The identity rows also derive the applied address from the pinned unapplied hash and one declared parameter, and forge an output at the canonical address with no token: the ledger accepts it and no script executed.

the-serialization-boundary-rows-devnet-s.text: One fresh cage per row: submitted datum bytes read back identical, one executing witness per spending redeemer constructor, a wrong constructor index refused by both cage scripts, request and mint constructors covered with the unreachable migration recorded, and the six-field token state round-tripped with the stake credential absent and present.

Every accepting row carries a skipped or corrupted variant the run requires to fail, and the refusal names every script that failed in ledger order. Had any verdict contradicted its contract it would be a finding, never relabelled.

the-serialization-checks-that-need-no-no.text: Thirteen Haskell encodings checked against the blueprint's own declared schemas read at run time, constructor by constructor with field order; parameter counts of one, two and zero with applied hashes derived in Haskell. Zero units honestly, measured sizes stated, and these rows never appear in a devnet-executed count.

cs07-unmarked-and-escalated.text: Branch and leaf proofs ride accepted folds, but no accepted fold has ever carried a fork, and two independently ground fork proofs verified by the Haskell stack are refused by the compiled validator with a bare machine error. The row carries no receipt and stays uncovered.
The full bundle of keys, shapes, both verdicts and the refusal bytes is filed as a user story escalation, and the offline oracle reproduces every offline claim without a node.

measurements.text: Ship run on a clean tree with cardano-node ten point seven. Maxima are queried from the running node, never hardcoded. Execution units stay under three percent for every row, and the forged payment reports zeros honestly because no script purpose exists to evaluate.

Serialized size is the tight dimension: about seventy percent of the transaction maximum for folds, about half for boots. The worst case across each session is recorded in that session's CL zero one receipt.
The serialization ship run names its own base with a clean tree. Its worst cases live in the row receipts: datum, witness and state folds beside the generic ones, size still the tight dimension.

what-this-slice-does-not-establish.text: Five rows rest on predecessor runs and are cited, not re-executed. The remaining uncovered rows include four expected consumer gaps that are recorded to observe, not passed.
The identity rows do not evidence the serialization boundary, constructor coverage or batch limits. Single-request devnet folds say nothing about other environments.

Row CS zero seven is unmarked with a finding, never a gap and never a pass. The migrating constructor is recorded unreachable with its validator-read reason. Refusal reasons keep every failing script hash in ledger order.

commands.text: List prints the inventory. Each session runs with its own command and a fresh receipts directory; a mixed request is refused. List against those receipts shows what executed.

Ten armed controls — the impossible marker twice, forged claims twice, the fabricated derivation, the naive authenticator, the unapplied address, the wrong index, the wrong parameters, corrupted bytes and the skipped witness — must each fail the run with a non-zero exit.

observed-environment.text: Observed with cardano-node ten point seven, GHC nine point twelve point three, and the Aiken compiler pinned by the blueprint, with the pinned unapplied hash and the applied hash recorded. Any other environment is explicitly not covered.
